text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000201 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity tier, but the few charts returned support the billed level, so the pattern cannot yet be distinguished from a genuinely complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel does skew complex, and most 99215s fall on multi-condition patients, such as sampled claim C0104160, whose chart documented high MDM. However, the 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every condition stratum, including patients with zero conditions, so panel acuity alone does not appear to explain the excess. Sampled low-complexity 99215s are the main concern: C0103880 and C0103939 are billed on patients with no chronic conditions and only a Z09 follow-up code, and C0103348 carries only unspecified abdominal pain (R10.9). Against this, the four documented 99215s were all supported and cloned-note signals were minimal, but records came back for a very small share of claims, so the documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215s, starting with the Z09-only and symptom-only visits listed, and then a larger random sample of 99215s from mid-complexity patients (2 to 3 conditions), where the excess over peers is substantial."}
